rationale: Recorded a negative result from the early reading so the account shows what was excluded and why: the handlePreAccept write that uses preAccept.LeaderId as the instance row looks like a reachable wrong-instance write, but its guard (Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil) is not produced by any writer in the captured package. The traced writer invariant is recorded as a behavior with sources, and the suspicion is registered under its own question as refuted with the conditions stated.

knowledge.statement: Every writer of an instance status at or above PREACCEPTED in the captured package installs a non-nil command in the same step: startPhase1 builds the instance with the batch it was given (and state.NOOP() when a recovery has no command), handlePreAccept sets inst.Cmds = preAccept.Command in the same branch that sets PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ, handlePreAcceptReply and handleTryPreAcceptReply copy lb.cmds, which those paths always hold, and handleTryPreAccept sets the command before setting PREACCEPTED. Acceptors that never pre-accepted report status NONE or PREACCEPTED(_EQ) and never ACCEPTED, because handleAccept records only bal, vbal, seq and deps.
knowledge.conditions: The captured snapshot's epaxos package with Thrifty on and IsLeader false, for any instance of any row (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779, 796-833, 895-960, 1204-1313, 1316-1352).

investigations.question: Can the handlePreAccept branch that writes r.InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][preAccept.Instance].Cmds run in the captured package, so that a recovery message can write the command into another instance's row or panic on a nil slot?
investigations.hypothesis: The branch requires a local instance with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil, and its write targets the row of preAccept.LeaderId at the instance index, which is a different instance whenever a recovering coordinator is the sender; if reachable, it would overwrite an unrelated instance's command or dereference a nil *Instance.
investigations.discriminator: Which writer can leave an instance at status ACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED with Cmds nil; tracing startPhase1, handlePreAccept, handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAccept and handleTryPreAcceptReply, together with the fact that handleAccept records no status, is what decides reachability.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the wrong-row write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 is latent rather than reachable in the captured package. The branch is entered only when inst.Status >= ACCEPTED and inst.Cmds == nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:807-808), and no writer traced in the package leaves an instance in that combination: startPhase1 always installs the batch it is given, replacing a nil command with state.NOOP() for recoveries (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779 and 1307-1313); handlePreAccept sets Cmds and the PREACCEPTED status in the same branch (epaxos/epaxos.go:815-833); handlePreAcceptReply copies lb.cmds, which is non-nil on that path (epaxos/epaxos.go:952-961); handleTryPreAccept sets the command before the status (epaxos/epaxos.go:1341-1345) and handleTryPreAcceptReply likewise carries lb.cmds; and acceptors that never pre-accepted report status NONE rather than ACCEPTED because handleAccept records only bal, vbal, seq and deps (epaxos/epaxos.go:985-1005), which is the same property that limits recovery's 'accepted' sub-case. The refutation is scoped to these writers in this snapshot: it does not rest on an unreachability proof for every possible interleaving, and it is the reason the write is recorded as a latent defect of the branch rather than a reported finding. Note also that the write itself is not merely a wrong index: for a recovering coordinator it targets the coordinator's own row at the instance number, so if some future change made a nil-command accepted state reachable, the effect would be either a nil-pointer panic or a command written into an unrelated instance.
counterevidence: The refutation depends on the writers traced here; a path that installs a status >= ACCEPTED without a command (for example a durable restart reconstructing state from the stable store, which is unreachable in this snapshot because Durable is hardcoded false) would defeat it.

handleAccept's lack of a status write is itself a deviation from the published protocol's ACCEPTED state, so a corrected implementation of the protocol would make this branch's premise easier to reach, not harder.
limitations: Source-only account: no execution exercised the branch, and the harnesses of this run never produced a status >= ACCEPTED instance without a command.
The trace covers the epaxos package's own writers; the master and the client packages cannot set instance statuses, and no other component in the captured tree writes InstanceSpace.

The branch's mis-indexing behaviour (row = LeaderId, index = Instance) was not exercised even in the non-recovering case, where LeaderId equals the instance's owner and the write would coincide with the intended slot.
